title: POC weekly ingress gate and telemetry runbook sync

Action items cover creds handoff, benchmark script, and follow-up security artifacts.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: Tue 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Rosa (Redwood SE), Evan (CSM), Evelyn (Mercury Head ML), Marc (Platform), Priya (Security), Tom (SRE)

Summary (auto): ingress gating, KV cache shadow bench scheduled, telemetry runbook handoff, security Q&A.

[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, um, quick agenda — ingress gating status, the telemetry runbook, and then the shadow bench for the KV cache. If we run out of time we'll pick SSO/KMS mapping at the end.
[00:18] Evelyn Santos: Yep sounds good. We have a tight window before compliance review so the gate stuff's priority.
[00:25] Rosa Kim: Quick reminder, the shadow bench is non-prod only, synthetic traffic, it won't touch PHI, we're just exercising prefix cache hit rates and tail latency.
[00:36] Marc Rivera: Right, just to confirm we need the IP ranges you'll be using and an ephemeral service account. Also want to understand the request patterns — are you doing continuous 200 qps or bursts?
[00:47] Rosa Kim: We're going to run a 10-minute ramp to 200 QPS, hold for 20, then ramp down. It's a bursty profile to exercise the batching paths and KV cache warmup.
[00:57] Tom Becker: Ok firewall team will need the probe IPs. Can you please send them as CIDR?
[01:05] Jordan Patel: Yes we'll send the list, that's on the runbook.
[01:12] Priya Nair: I have a couple security items — SSO and KMS. We can't share keys, obviously, so we'll need guidance for using your customer-managed KMS pass-through or using our HSM. Also SOC2 artifacts, where do we get those?
[01:29] Evan Brooks: We can drop over our SOC2 type II report and a security pack, and Rosa is the best to walk the KMS integration patterns with you.
[01:36] Rosa Kim: For KMS we support two patterns: 1) Bring-your-own KMS — you manage keys and we do envelope encryption, or 2) you provide wrapped keys via an HSM connector. There are some minor network requirements for the key exchange call.
[01:54] Priya Nair: When you say "minor" do you mean inbound or outbound requests from our VPC?
[01:59] Rosa Kim: Outbound. We make a signed call to the key broker endpoint during startup, typically TLS only. That can be tunneled via private link, we have docs. Sorry if that wasn't clear earlier; earlier notes said private link but we often use egress over VPC peering at customers.
[02:17] Evelyn Santos: Ok. For the bench, we also want to measure token-level cost differences between quantized and float models. Is that part of the script?
[02:25] Rosa Kim: We can add two runs — one with int8 quant and one with FP16 — same prompt distribution. The bench will report latency P50/P95 and per-token compute ms and approximate token cost.
[02:36] Marc Rivera: Note that our billing team might need a mapping of calls to cost buckets. Can you surface token counts and model variant per call?
[02:44] Jordan Patel: Yep, we can emit a CSV with per-request token counts and model id, and correlate to the telemetry traces.
[02:51] 
[03:05] -- Topics: ingress creds status, bench schedule, telemetry and alerts, SSO/KMS Q&A --
[03:13] Marc Rivera: Quick update from our side: VPC peering is provisioned but needs the peer ASN and the exact subnet ranges, we'll attach a ticket.
[03:22] Jordan Patel: I'll paste the peer netblocks and ASN after the call.
[03:28] Tom Becker: Also we need a fail-open fallback plan: if the KV cache warms slowly, we need graceful degradation to avoid 10s of seconds latency spikes. What's Redwood's fallback?
[03:40] Rosa Kim: We do prefix caching and automatic fallback to smaller model variants and — if configured — a rate-limited circuit breaker. We can keep a canary route to a lower-cost model to preserve throughput. There is some nuance: tradeoffs are cost vs latency.
[03:55] Evelyn Santos: Does that mean in practice if the cache misses we go to an FP16 model and accept slightly higher token compute?
[04:03] Rosa Kim: It could be either fallback to FP16 or to a smaller architecture depending on your config. We'll demo the rule set in the runbook.
[04:10] Marc Rivera: Important for us: we need deterministic routing rules — ops folks don't want surprises in production.
[04:17] Jordan Patel: We provide a routing policy DSL you can pin — canary percentages and absolute fallback thresholds, and we log decisions in traces for audit.
[04:26] Priya Nair: Audit logs are great — are these integrated with our SIEM via syslog/Firehose?
[04:33] Rosa Kim: Yes we have a delivery to S3/CloudWatch/Kinesis and you can forward to your SIEM. There is a retention policy parameter in the console.
[04:44] Tom Becker: What's the minimum retention you can set if compliance asks?
[04:47] Evan Brooks: We support rolling windows down to 30 days for standard plans; enterprise can request longer. We'll add that detail to the security pack.
[04:57] 
[05:12] -- Timestamp jump, mid-call bench planning --
[05:20] Rosa Kim: For the bench we'll need traces instrumented with request id, model id, token counts, and cache-hit flag. The script tags each request with a small synthetic header so you can filter.
[05:33] Marc Rivera: We'll need an example trace format, can you send one?
[05:36] Rosa Kim: Yes, the bench repo includes synthetic traces and a parsing notebook. I'll attach the link.
[05:42] Evelyn Santos: A note on evaluation: our ML team wants to see quality A/B between quantized and non-quantized models using a fixed test set of 200 prompts. Can you run that as well?
[05:52] Rosa Kim: Absolutely — we'll run the eval set and report BLEU-ish metrics and prompt-anchored scoring. Note that some evals are heuristic; we'll put human review notes where applicable.
[06:06] Priya Nair: Another security question: SAML SSO mapping — we use attributes for team and role; can you ingest arbitrary SAML attributes for RBAC?
[06:15] Jordan Patel: Yes, we map SAML assertions to RBAC roles. There is a small mapping table we update in the console. We'll need a sample assertion to validate.
[06:25] Priya Nair: We can provide that. Also note our security team requires the KMS key policy to prevent Redwood staff from accessing raw keys. Is that supported?
[06:35] Rosa Kim: Yes we support key policies that restrict Redwood personnel. That is standard for private deployments and for dedicated instances we can lock access controls.
[06:45] 
[07:00] Marc Rivera: About telemetry alerts — what are default thresholds? We need early warning for P95 > 350ms and for error rate > 0.5%
[07:09] Evan Brooks: Default thresholds are conservative, we can ship a runbook with suggested thresholds and notification playbooks. We'll include Grafana dashboards and example alert rules.
[07:19] Rosa Kim: Also we'll add an automated alert that triggers when cache hit ratio drops below X% for Y minutes so you can catch regressions.
[07:27] 
[07:40] Evelyn Santos: Let's talk timeline — compliance review on 2026-07-10. We need the SOC2 and runbook before that.
[07:47] Jordan Patel: We'll send the SOC2 bundle and telemetry runbook draft by 2026-07-02. Bench window scheduled 2026-07-01 02:00-05:00 UTC pending your ephemeral creds.
[07:57] Priya Nair: We'll try to provision the service account and firewall rules by 2026-07-01 EOD. If we can't, please postpone the bench.
[08:06] Jordan Patel: Noted.
[08:12] 
[08:30] -- Mid-call interjection about cost estimates --
[08:35] Marc Rivera: One more from finance — can you give a per-token estimate for the quant vs non-quant runs? We need to ballpark cost to a thousand users.
[08:46] Jordan Patel: We'll provide a cost sensitivity table; rough numbers in the runbook and a dedicated pricing sheet.
[08:52] 
[09:05] Rosa Kim: Small gotcha I want to flag: if the bench uses short prompts the batching window will be small; we may not reach ideal GPU utilization. For cost comparisons please include a profile with average prompt length ~45 tokens.
[09:18] Evelyn Santos: Good point — our user distribution median is 38 tokens but mean is 60 so include both.
[09:25] 
[09:40] -- Security deep-dive scheduling --
[09:44] Priya Nair: Once we get your sample assertion and the SOC2, we'll set a 30-minute mapping call next week.
[09:52] Jordan Patel: Rosa and I available Tue or Wed morning PST.
[09:58] Priya Nair: Wed fine.
[10:03] 
[10:10] -- Closing recap and explicit next steps --
[10:12] Jordan Patel: Recap: 1) Bench scheduled 2026-07-01 02:00-05:00 UTC, pending creds from Marc and Tom. 2) Redwood will send SOC2 and telemetry runbook draft by 2026-07-02. 3) Rosa will deliver bench script and example traces by tomorrow. 4) Security deep-dive Wed next week.
[10:33] Evelyn Santos: That covers it. Thanks all.
[10:38] Tom Becker: Thanks.
[10:40] Jordan Patel: Thanks folks, we'll follow up with links and the runbook. Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: some speakers overlap, occasional mis-typed words ("KV cash" in export), proper nouns sometimes mis-cased.
